arxiv-1809-01796.title: Optimal Sparse Singular Value Decomposition for High-dimensional High-order Data
arxiv-1809-01796.creator: Anru Zhang, Rungang Han
arxiv-1809-01796.description: Abstract In this article, we consider the sparse tensor singular value decomposition, which aims for dimension reduction on high-dimensional high-order data with certain sparsity structure. A method named s parse t ensor a lternating t hresholding for s ingular v alue d ecomposition (STAT-SVD) is proposed.

arxiv-2111-08864.title: Adversarial Tradeoffs in Robust State Estimation
arxiv-2111-08864.creator: Thomas T.C.K. Zhang, Bruce D. Lee, Hamed Hassani, Nikolai Matni
arxiv-2111-08864.description: Abstract Adversarially robust training has been shown to reduce the susceptibility of learned models to targeted input data perturbations. However, it has also been observed that such adversarially robust models suffer a degradation in accuracy when applied to unperturbed data sets, leading to a robustness-accuracy tradeoff.

arxiv-2202-11502.title: Graphs of continuous functions and fractal dimension Thanks: …
arxiv-2202-11502.creator: Manuj Verma, Amit Priyadarshi
arxiv-2202-11502.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Manuj Verma, Amit Priyadarshi. In this paper, we show that, for any β ∈ [ 1 , 2 ] \beta\in[1,2] , a given strictly positive real-valued continuous function on [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] whose graph has upper box-counting dimension less than or equal to β \beta can be decomposed as a product of two real-valued continuous functions on [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] whose graphs have upper box-counting dimension equal to β \beta .

arxiv-2305-11298.title: Precision versus Shrinkage: A Comparative Analysis of Covariance Estimation Methods for Portfolio Allocation
arxiv-2305-11298.creator: Sumanjay Dutta, Shashi Jain
arxiv-2305-11298.description: Abstract In this paper, we perform a comprehensive study of different covariance and precision matrix estimation methods in the context of minimum variance portfolio allocation. The set of models studied by us can be broadly categorized as: Gaussian Graphical Model (GGM) based methods, Shrinkage Methods, Thresholding and Random Matrix Theory (RMT) based methods.

arxiv-2405-08075.title: Identification of non-isomorphic 2 2 -groups with dihedral central quotient and isomorphic modular group algebras
arxiv-2405-08075.creator: Leo Margolis, Taro Sakurai
arxiv-2405-08075.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Leo Margolis, Taro Sakurai. The question whether non-isomorphic finite p p -groups can have isomorphic modular group algebras was recently answered in the negative by García-Lucas, Margolis and del Río [J. We embed these negative solutions in the class of two-generated finite 2 2 -groups with dihedral central quotient, and solve the original question for all groups within this class. As a result, we discover new negative solutions and simple algebra isomorphisms.

arxiv-2410-10014.title: Safety-Aware Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
arxiv-2410-10014.creator: Hyeong Kyu Choi, Xuefeng Du, Yixuan Li
arxiv-2410-10014.description: Abstract Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) has emerged as a common practice for tailoring models to individual needs and preferences. The choice of datasets for fine-tuning can be diverse, introducing safety concerns regarding the potential inclusion of harmful data samples. Manually filtering or avoiding such samples, however, can be labor-intensive and subjective.

arxiv-2509-24559.title: Emergent World Representations in OpenVLA
arxiv-2509-24559.creator: Marco Molinari, Leonardo Nevali, Saharsha Navani, Omar Younis
arxiv-2509-24559.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marco Molinari, Leonardo Nevali, Saharsha Navani, Omar Younis. Vision Language Action models (VLAs) trained with policy-based reinforcement learning (RL) encode complex behaviors without explicitly modeling environmental dynamics. However, it remains unclear whether VLAs implicitly learn world models, a hallmark of model-based RL. We propose an experimental methodology using embedding arithmetic on state representations to probe whether OpenVLA, the current state of the art in VLAs, contains latent knowledge of state transitions.

pmc-11645690.creator: D Bird, D Curtin, G Tay
pmc-11645690.description: Introduction/AimApproximately 25% of patients with GOLD stage 3 or 4 COPD have chronic hypercapnia with a daytime/awake PaCO2 >45mmHg. Persistent hypercapnia is associated with worse quality of life, increased frequency and severity of exacerbations, increased frequency and length of hospital presentations, increased need for invasive and non-invasive acute non-invasive ventilation (NIV) and increased mortality.

pmc-11678063.title: The Search for a Universal Treatment for Defined and Mixed Pathology Neurodegenerative Diseases
pmc-11678063.creator: Danton H O’Day
pmc-11678063.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The predominant neurodegenerative diseases, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, dementia with Lewy Bodies, Huntington’s disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and frontotemporal dementia, are rarely pure diseases but, instead, show a diversity of mixed pathologies. At some level, all of them share a combination of one or more different toxic biomarker proteins: amyloid beta (Aβ), phosphorylated Tau (pTau), alpha-synuclein (αSyn), mutant huntingtin (mHtt), fused in sarcoma, superoxide dismutase 1, and TAR DNA-binding protein 43.
